name: Week 15 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Chest-Supported Row + Face Pull)
description: Volume steady. The behind-back shrug moves to an early activation slot — it's protective 'opposite movement' work for the right shoulder, and burying it as the closing station last week meant a rushed session dropped it (the shoulder flared). Chest-supported row steps up to 40 (35 was too easy two weeks running). Face pull gets the spotlight refresh now that the elbows-high / external-rotate cue is landing. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option, including the new dual-pulley variant.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Behind-back shrug moves to the FRONT of the session as protective activation. Chest-supported row steps to 40. Face pull gets the spotlight. DB row holds the 60/70/80 pyramid, pull-ups hold 4 sets. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: 35 came in 'too easy without a sweat' two weeks running, so the weight-up is earned — steps to 40. Spotlight drills the chest-glued-to-bench / elbow-to-hip cue at the new load so the form holds through the jump, not just the number.

Cycles back — last spotlighted W12. The reposted form (elbows high above the shoulders, external-rotate at the top) just started landing — 'very different, feeling it in the back.' Spotlight locks that cue in at 42.5 before any load change.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W12 face pull + reverse fly · W13 bicep + high cable curl + cable crunch · W14 pull-up + DB row · W15 chest-supported row + face pull (current) · W16 cycle forward — lat pulldown or bicep refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug is now FIRST (activation slot), not the closing station.** It's protective decompression work — the counter-movement to all the pulling — and it's the one piece that can't be allowed to drop. Do it right after the warmup. (The shrug/trap-3 alternation pauses this week; the shrug specifically is the protective piece, so it stays.) A light 1-set version is now also greased into the push + KB-day warmups.
**Chest-supported row steps to 40.** Confirm the form holds through the jump — chest glued, elbow to the hip, no torso twist. If 40 grinds the form, drop back to 35 and we hold.

**Shoulder management:** last week's flare was VOLUME-driven (more sets, all slow-eccentric, high time-under-tension), not weight. Don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once — ramp the tempo. Lean on the early shrug, the cable fly, morning stretches, and external rotations. The flare is management-tractable as long as the shrug actually gets done.
**Loads hold** — DB row 60/70/80, pull-up bodyweight, face pull 42.5, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20. Cable crunch steps up (see its notes).
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick whichever station's free, log equipment + number. Lat pulldown now has four known variants (machine / cable column / cable pulley / dual pulley).
**Left bicep first, every set** — the weak-left pattern resurfaces when the curl comes late in the session.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 in push warmup + 1-2 in KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — moved to the FRONT this week.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Burying it at the end meant it got skipped, and the shoulder flared. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point. Do it before the loaded pulling so it's locked in.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades together at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

**Reflection:** does doing the shrug first change how the right shoulder feels through the rest of the pull session vs. the weeks it was last or skipped?

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, moved to the front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — treat it as a decompression, not a max effort. This is the full 3-set version; a light 1-set greasing version now also lives in the push + KB-day warmups.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. Don't grind to failure with the shoulder freshly out of last week's flare; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row (Spotlight) + DB Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40 (step up from 35 — it was too easy two weeks running). 3 sets of 10-12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the form holds at the new load:**
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs up, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — elbow-to-hip keeps it in the lats, not the rear delt
- **Don't rotate the torso** — no twisting up to throw the DB; both sides of the chest stay on the pad
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull

**Reflection:** does 40 still hold the chest-glued, elbow-to-hip form for all 3 clean sets, or does the form start cheating (chest peels, torso twists) on set 3? If the form cheats, that's the ceiling — drop to 35 and we hold there.

**LOAD:** 60/70/80 ascending pyramid — one set per round (60, then 70, then 80). 80 holds clean now, so the pyramid stays.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting up
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze**
- **At 80:** if the torso starts twisting or the elbow drifts to the armpit, stop the set — that's the form tapping out.

**LOAD:** 25lb. 3 sets of 8-10. Preacher-style chest-supported curl (the preacher-bench replacement).
- **Set the incline bench to ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad
- **Arm hangs down the face of the pad**, underhand grip; the upper arm stays flat on the pad the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow off)
- **Left arm first, every set** — the weak-left pattern returns when the curl comes late
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — strict tempo, cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing extra reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench)
- DBs hanging fully extended at the start, **soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive**
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep, don't lift
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — no swing

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Dual pulley: 70** ('surprisingly strong' here)
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- 'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets' at the bottom
- 1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return to a full overhead stretch
- Knees pinned firmly under the pad

**LOAD:** cable column 42.5. 3 sets of 20.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — lock in the cue that just started landing:**
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moved the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold** at the contracted position
- **Slow controlled return, 2s** — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- This is rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of the pull day

**Reflection:** can you keep 'feeling it in the back' (not the front of the shoulder / the biceps) for all 3 sets at 42.5? If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped — re-set them high. Hold 42.5 while the cue is the focus.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 75-77.5** (step up — 72.5 came in 'fairly easy')
- **Cable column (rope): 135**

3 sets.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric.** If the step-up still feels easy, note it for another bump.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug moves to FIRST** — protective decompression for the right shoulder. It can't be the piece a rushed session drops anymore.
**Chest-supported row steps to 40** — 35 was too easy two weeks running. Spotlight: confirm the form holds through the jump.
**Face pull spotlight** — elbows high, external-rotate, feel it in the back. Hold 42.5 and lock the cue.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. Last week's flare was volume/TUT, not weight.
**Loads hold** — DB row 60/70/80 pyramid, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20.
**Cable crunch steps up to pulley 75-77.5** (72.5 was fairly easy).
**Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers** — lat pulldown (140 machine / 70 dual pulley / 52.5-57.5 column / 47.5 pulley). Pick what's free, log it.
**Left bicep first, every set** — weak-left pattern.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with one structural change: the protective shrug leads instead of trails, because the shoulder needs the decompression work front-loaded and reliably done. Chest-supported row earns its weight-up after two easy weeks; face pull earns the spotlight now that its cue finally landed. Loads otherwise hold — last week's flare was volume, not weight, so the lever is sequencing and tempo, not backing off the numbers. Building decades, not weeks.
